Meta.title: {brand}: robotics kits for primary to senior high
Meta.description: Robotics kits that students build and program, a free in-browser simulator, a meeting-by-meeting curriculum, and teacher support for schools across Indonesia.

Common.conceptNote: Images are concept renders. The final product may differ.

Arena.label: Animation of a robot following a black line with two sensors
Arena.caption: Two sensors under the robot read the black line. When one sensor touches it, the robot turns that way. That is how SD v1 learns to follow a track.

hero.title: <line>Build the robot.</line> <line>Teach it to think.</line>
hero.body: Robotics kits for primary, junior high, and senior high, with a free simulator and a meeting-by-meeting curriculum. Students build, program, test, and fix real robots.
hero.note: The simulator runs in the browser, no sign-up.

kits.title: Three kits, one way of learning
kits.intro: From primary to senior high, students learn the same way: simulate, build, program, test. The challenge is what grows.

path.title: One meeting, four steps
path.intro: Every mission is tried in the simulator, then taken to the real robot. If the robot fails at step four, that is not the end. It is data for the next fix.

simulate.title: Try it in the simulator
simulate.body: Snap blocks together and run the mission in the browser. Mistakes here break nothing.

build.title: Get the robot ready
build.body: SD v1 arrives ready to use. Students build SMP v1 and SMA v1 from modules, with no soldering.

program.title: Move the program over
program.body: Blocks for primary, blocks then C++ for junior high, Python and ROS 2 for senior high.

test.title: Test, measure, fix
test.body: A classroom floor is not the simulator. Students record results, find the cause, and try again.

upgrades.title: The robot levels up too
upgrades.intro: Upgrade packs add new abilities, and new projects, to the robots a school already owns. No need to start again with a new robot.

sim.title: Try it in the browser first, for free
sim.body: The simulator mimics the real robot’s sensors and motors. Twelve missions follow the primary and junior high curriculum modules, and every program has a C++ view.
sim.imageAlt: The simulator: program blocks on the left, the robot arena and sensor panel on the right

curriculum.title: A meeting-by-meeting curriculum, ready for class
curriculum.intro: Each square is one meeting, and its colour marks the module. Hover or tap a square to see its title.
curriculum.kka: Lessons map to the elective Coding and Artificial Intelligence subject.

schools.title: Start with one class
schools.intro: A pilot lets a school try the robots, the curriculum, and teacher training in one class before rolling out further.

trial.title: Try the simulator with teachers
trial.body: We sit with your teachers as they try missions in the school computer lab.

training.title: Teacher training
training.body: One hands-on session: preparing robots, running a meeting, and assessing student work.

class.title: Pilot in one class
class.body: Robots, guides, and support for one class over several meetings.

review.title: Review, then expand
review.body: We review the learning results together, then agree on robots and schedules for other classes.

Kits.metaTitle: SD v1, SMP v1, and SMA v1 robotics kits
Kits.metaDescription: Compare the robotics kits for primary, junior high, and senior high: how they are built, controllers, programming, curriculum, and status.
Kits.title: A robotics kit for every level
Kits.intro: Each kit comes with its own robot, simulator missions, and curriculum. Kit names carry a version number, so the next kit is easy to tell apart.

Kit.noUpgrades: Upgrades for this kit are being prepared.
Kit.modularBody: Modules plug in and out through keyed connectors, so the same robot becomes a line follower, an obstacle avoider, a voice-controlled robot, or a monitoring station.
Kit.pcb: The custom PCB every module connects to
Kit.developmentNote: {kit} is still in development. The specification and box contents may change before it goes on sale.

Upgrades.metaDescription: Upgrade packs add new abilities and projects to school robotics kits: remote control, sensors, gripper, camera, arena, and competition prep.
Upgrades.title: Upgrade packs and accessories
Upgrades.intro: School robots can keep growing. Upgrade packs add abilities and projects; accessories keep the class running smoothly.
Upgrades.note: Upgrade packs and accessories are still in development. Contents and availability may change.

Curriculum.metaDescription: A 32-meeting primary robotics syllabus and 36-meeting junior and senior high syllabi, with goals, evidence of learning, rubrics, and KKA mapping.
Curriculum.title: Curriculum and syllabus
Curriculum.intro: Every level has modules, a per-meeting plan, evidence of learning, and an assessment rubric.
Curriculum.kkaIntro: The Coding and Artificial Intelligence elements this level strengthens most.
Curriculum.tiersIntro: Variations of activity on the same robot, not three different devices.
Curriculum.rubricIntro: Assess the process, not only whether the first program worked.

Guides.metaDescription: Guides to start a kit, run a robotics class, assemble SMP v1, stay safe with batteries, and use the simulator.
Guides.title: Guides
Guides.intro: Practical steps for teachers, students, and schools.

Simulator.metaDescription: Try SD v1 and SMP v1 missions in the browser: motion, line sensors, distance, servo radar, temperature, and sound, with a C++ preview.
Simulator.title: A robot simulator, free in the browser
Simulator.intro: Schools can try every mission before buying a robot. The simulator mimics the real robot’s sensors, motors, and screen.

features.physics: Two-wheel motion: speed, turning, and the difference between left and right motors
features.line: Two-point line sensing on SD v1 and five-point on SMP v1
features.distance: Ultrasonic distance, including on a servo
features.outputs: Faces and text on the OLED screen, and the buzzer
features.env: Temperature, humidity, and claps for SMP v1 missions
features.code: A C++ preview of the blocks you build

Simulator.trialBody: Want the simulator in your computer lab with missions made for your school? We set up access and a short training for teachers.

Schools.metaDescription: Pilot programmes, classroom sets, teacher training, after-sales support, custom kits, and robotics competition prep for schools.
Schools.title: The programme for schools
Schools.intro: We do not just ship kits. We prepare how to teach with them, train the teachers, and support the class.
Schools.pilotIntro: The safest way to start: one class, one semester, results you can assess together.
Schools.classTitle: How many robots a class needs
Schools.classBody: We suggest one robot for two to three students, rotating roles: programmer, tester, and recorder. A class of 30 needs 10 to 15 robots.
Schools.customIntro: Kits, curriculum, and simulator missions can be tailored to your school or organisation.
Schools.competitionsBody: Advanced material and the Competition Pack are prepared for teams heading to {list}.
Schools.ctaBody: Student numbers, levels, and the lesson timetable help us put together the right proposal.

Contact.metaDescription: Request a proposal for robotics kits, a pilot programme, or simulator trial access for your school.
Contact.title: Request a school proposal
Contact.intro: Fill in the form, then send it by WhatsApp or email. We reply with a proposal and a demo schedule.
